coordinate_convention: All landmarks use uncropped source pixels unless explicitly marked recovered_crop_coordinates; manually estimated feature boxes are approximate, not segmentation ground truth.

kneeling.preferred_transform: one common uniform scale across all source-native crops; one fixed knee-contact anchor; no independent fit-to-width

preview_starting_point_only.padding_intent: approximately 40px horizontal and at least 24px vertical, recompute over cleaned visible alpha union before finalizing

intrinsic_caveats: Male frame2 has a much straighter knee/leg silhouette than other kneeling frames; source recovery does not change this anatomy.
Frames0 and3 are separately drawn start-like poses, so head/arm/plate details are not pixel-identical loop endpoints.
Rolling toward the three-quarter camera can legitimately increase projected plate size; do not erase that perspective merely to equalize equipment bounding boxes.

standing.preferred_transform: manual small per-frame uniform scale calibration using equipment plus athlete landmarks; stationary toe/forefoot contact anchor; then one common final scale fitted to the union
intrinsic_caveats: Per-frame plate/athlete proportions and viewpoint vary; a single translation cannot fix those variations.
Uniform scale corrections stabilize one chosen reference but cannot make independently redrawn body proportions and equipment identical simultaneously.
The wheel is a moving exercise element and must not be used as the fixed horizontal anchor.
Toe versus heel contact changes across the action; anchor the supporting forefoot rather than the rightmost or lowest overall-alpha pixel.

alpha_requirement: Preserve input alpha by multiplying the cleanup mask with original alpha. In recovered kneeling crops, hidden RGB outside the manual polygon still contains neighboring sprites; converting to RGB and regenerating alpha would resurrect them.
safe_transform_formula: p_out = shared_scale * per_frame_uniform_calibration * (p_source_or_crop - frame_anchor) + common_canvas_anchor. Compute transformed visible-alpha bounds for all four frames; reduce shared_scale once if any frame exceeds padding. Never independently rescale each frame to fit its own box.
